items.title: Section: Fascicle 46 Opens — the Fifteenth and Final Topic, the Four Dharma-Summaries Named as the Classical Four Seals

items.zh: 復有四種法嗢拕南，諸佛菩薩欲令有情清淨故說。何等為四？一切諸行皆是無常，是名第一法嗢拕南。一切諸行皆悉是苦，是名第二法嗢拕南。一切諸法皆無有我，是名第三法嗢拕南。涅槃寂靜，是名第四法嗢拕南。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter seventeen, part three: the factors of awakening. There are, further, four dharma-summaries, spoken by every buddha and bodhisattva in order to purify beings. What are these four? All conditioned activities are impermanent — this is called the first dharma-summary. All conditioned activities are suffering — this is called the second dharma-summary. All phenomena are without self — this is called the third dharma-summary. Nirvāṇa is peace — this is called the fourth dharma-summary.

items.title: Section: Three Meanings of "Udāna" — Correspondence With Reality, the Buddhas' Own Constant Repetition, and the Very Path That Leads Beyond Existence Itself

items.zh: 諸佛菩薩多為有情宣說如是法相應義，是故說名法嗢拕南。又從曩昔，其心寂靜諸牟尼尊，於一切時展轉宣說，是故說此名嗢拕南。又此行迹能趣大生，亦復能趣出第一有，是故說此名嗢拕南。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas, teaching beings this meaning that genuinely corresponds to the dharma, are for this reason said to speak a dharma-summary. Furthermore, since time immemorial, the sages whose minds have become genuinely still have, at every time, repeatedly proclaimed this same teaching — this is why it is called a dharma-summary. Furthermore, this very track leads towards favourable rebirth, and is likewise able to lead one entirely beyond the very highest state of existence — this is why it is called a dharma-summary.

items.title: Section: Impermanence Opens — No Conditioned Activity Ever Possessed a Fixed Verbal Essence in the First Place, Across Four Rising Levels of Genuine Reality

items.zh: 云何菩薩等隨觀察一切諸行皆是無常？謂諸菩薩，觀一切行言說自性，於一切時常無所有。如是諸行常不可得，故名無常。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas universally and thoroughly observe that all conditioned activities are impermanent? Bodhisattvas who observe that the verbally-labelled essence of every conditioned activity is, at all times, never actually present at all — since these conditioned activities are thus always ungraspable in this sense, this is called impermanence.

items.title: Section: Moment-to-Moment Arising — Every Conditioned Activity Is Genuinely New, Never the Same Instant Twice

items.zh: 又即觀彼離言說事，由不了知彼真實故；無知為因，生滅可得。如是諸行離言自性有生有滅，故名無常。
items.en: Furthermore, observing this same matter beyond words, since its genuine reality is not understood, ignorance becomes the cause through which arising and ceasing become apparent. In this way, the wordless essence of conditioned activities genuinely has both arising and ceasing — this is why it is called impermanence.

items.title: Section: Neither Cause Nor Effect Genuinely Persists — Observing Impermanence Across Past, Present, and Future

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，觀過去行已生已滅，由彼諸行無因可得，亦無自性，是故觀彼因性、自性皆無所有。觀現在行已生未滅，由彼諸行因不可得，已與果故；自性可得，猶未滅故；是故觀彼自性是有，而無有因。觀未來行未生未滅，由彼諸行有因可得，未與果故；無有自性，猶未生故；是故觀彼唯有因性，而無自性。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas observe that past conditioned activities have already arisen and already ceased; since their cause is no longer to be found, and they possess no nature of their own any longer, one observes that both their causal quality and their own nature are entirely absent. One observes that present conditioned activities have already arisen but have not yet ceased; since their cause cannot be found, having already produced its result, yet their own nature can still be found, not having ceased as yet, one observes that their nature exists, though no cause remains. One observes that future conditioned activities have not yet arisen and have not yet ceased; since their cause can still be found, not having yet produced its result, yet they possess no nature of their own, not having yet arisen, one observes that only their causal quality is present, with no nature yet to be found.

items.title: Section: The Finer Analysis Opens — Death and Rebirth as Simultaneous as the Two Ends of a Scale, and Four Marks Packed Into a Single Instant

items.zh: 菩薩如是見三世中分段諸行相續轉已，等隨觀見一一剎那有為諸行，皆有三種有為之相。於剎那後，復有第四有為之相。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, having thus seen how conditioned activities, divided into segments across the three times, continue on in succession, universally and thoroughly observe that each and every instant of conditioned activity possesses three marks of conditioned existence; and, immediately following that same instant, there is a fourth mark of conditioned existence as well.

items.title: Section: Birth, Abiding, Ageing, and Cessation Defined — Four Angles on One and the Same Fleeting Instant, Never Four Separate Substances

items.zh: 即於此中，前剎那行自性滅壞。無間非先諸行剎那自性生起。正觀為生；諸行生已，即時未壞，正觀為住；此已生行，望前已滅諸行剎那自性別異，正觀為老；從此諸行生剎那後，即此已生諸行剎那自性滅壞，正觀為滅。菩薩觀此已生剎那諸行自性，即是生住老之自性，不見生等別有自性。如實觀見生剎那後，即此生等諸行剎那自性滅壞，無別有性。如是四種有為之相，總攝諸行。
items.en: Within this very instant, the previous instant's own nature having already perished, the uninterrupted arising, immediately following, of a conditioned activity's own genuinely new instantaneous nature is correctly observed as birth. That same conditioned activity, having arisen, not yet having perished, is correctly observed as abiding. This same already-arisen activity, differing in its instantaneous nature from the previously ceased activity, is correctly observed as ageing. Following this very instant of the activity's arising, that same already-arisen activity's own instantaneous nature perishing is correctly observed as cessation. Bodhisattvas observe that this already-arisen instantaneous activity's own nature is nothing other than the very nature of birth, abiding, and ageing themselves, seeing no separate nature belonging to birth and the rest apart from the activity. They correctly and genuinely observe that, following the instant of birth, this same activity's own instantaneous nature of birth and the rest simply perishes, with no separate nature involved. These four marks of conditioned existence together comprehend the entirety of conditioned activity.

items.title: Section: Why the Buddha Sometimes Teaches Three Marks Instead of Four — Merging Abiding Into Ageing, or Ageing Into Abiding

items.zh: 以要言之，二分所顯。一者、有分所顯。二者、無分所顯。此中世尊依於有分，建立一種有為之相；依於無分，建立第二有為之相。住、異二種，俱是諸行有分所顯，建立第三有為之相。
items.en: In brief, this is disclosed through two divisions: first, what is disclosed through having a share; second, what is disclosed through having no share. Here, the World-Honoured One, based on what has a share, establishes one mark of conditioned existence; based on what has no share, establishes a second mark of conditioned existence. Abiding and ageing, both being disclosed through what has a share belonging to conditioned activities, together establish the third mark of conditioned existence.

items.title: Section: Refuting a Separate, Substantial "Arising" Behind Arising Itself — Debating the Sarvāstivāda School

items.zh: 此中菩薩，觀一切時唯有諸行，除此更無生住老滅恒有實物自性成就。何以故？諸行生時，唯即如是諸行可得，無別有餘生住老滅。如是諸行住老滅時，唯即如是諸行可得，無別有餘生住老滅。
items.en: Here, bodhisattvas observe that, at all times, only conditioned activities themselves are found; beyond this, there is no separately, permanently existing real substance called arising, abiding, ageing, or cessation. Why is this so? When conditioned activities arise, only these very activities are found, with no separate arising, abiding, ageing, or cessation beyond them. Likewise, when these same conditioned activities abide, age, or cease, only these very activities are found, with no separate arising, abiding, ageing, or cessation beyond them.

items.title: Section: The Absurdity of Two Births, and the Dilemma of Sameness or Difference — Classical Objections to a Real Entity Called "Birth"

items.zh: 又諸菩薩以理推求生等實物亦不可得。如是推求不可得者，謂若離彼色等諸行別有生法，是即應如色等諸行自體有生。如是此生亦應有生。如是即應有二種生，一者、行生，二者、生生。如是行生與彼生生為一為異？若言一者，計生實有即為唐捐。言別有生是實物有，不應道理。若言異者，如是即應非行生生；是行生生，不應道理。如說生相，如是廣說住老滅相，當知亦爾。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, seeking through reasoning, find that no genuine substance corresponding to birth and the rest can be found either. That is to say, if there genuinely existed, apart from form and the other conditioned activities, a separate entity called birth, then just as form and the other activities themselves are born, this very birth would itself also need to be born — producing exactly two kinds of birth: first, the birth of the activity; second, the birth of birth itself. Are this birth of the activity and this birth of birth identical or different? If identical, then positing birth as a genuinely separate real entity accomplishes nothing at all — this is unreasonable. If different, then the activity's birth would then not actually be a birth belonging to that activity at all — yet it is said to be the activity's own birth, which is likewise unreasonable. Exactly as stated regarding the mark of birth, so too, in full, regarding the marks of abiding, ageing, and cessation — one should understand these in exactly the same way.

blocks.text: Fascicle 46 opens with the last of the fifteen topics of the factors-of-awakening chapter: the four dharma-summaries, known today as the "four seals". Today: what an udāna is, and impermanence analysed down to the single instant.

"All conditioned activities are impermanent; all conditioned activities are suffering; all phenomena are without self; nirvāṇa is peace." Master Cháng Bǎi: impermanence marks the conditioned, suffering the tainted, non-self all phenomena, and peace the unconditioned. The old word "udāna" means the defining, unchanging mark of the Dharma, now translated "dharma seal"; it gathers many teachings into a few words so learners can take them in easily.

It teaches meaning in accord with the Dharma; the sages of still mind have always repeated it; and this track leads to the great birth and beyond the highest existence. Venerable Miào Jìng: "muni" means stillness; a "track" is the footprints left on the road you have walked. "Leading to the great birth" means attaining acceptance of non-arising and supreme awakening; the "highest existence" is the peak of the formless realm.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the past having perished, neither cause nor result is findable; the present has its result, the cause already spent; the future has its cause, the result not yet produced, "as a seed becomes a sprout, and the sprout is no longer the seed."

Master Cháng Bǎi: at death, death and birth are simultaneous, like the two ends of a scale going down and up at the same moment, or like pushing a revolving door: this life's aggregates pass into the past as the next life's come forward.
"This already-arisen activity, differing from the previously ceased instant, is correctly observed as ageing." Venerable Miào Jìng: everything appearing is new; nothing is old.
When the sūtras say "birth, change, cessation", abiding has been merged into change (both lecturers). Master Cháng Bǎi: change and cessation look alike, but change has marks while cessation has none.

The treatise argues against the Sarvāstivāda view that birth is a real entity. Master Cháng Bǎi: they call the birth of an activity the "great birth" and the birth of that birth the "small birth". Venerable Miào Jìng: in their view even the great birth has its own substance, which the treatise rejects.
"Everything appearing is new, nothing old." Try noticing this for a minute: a breath, a sound, a thought. Each is gone as it appears. That is the first seal, seen directly.

options: all formations impermanent, all formations suffering, all phenomena selfless, nirvāṇa is peace
quiz.why: All conditioned activities are impermanent; all conditioned activities are suffering; all phenomena are without self; nirvāṇa is peace. Master Cháng Bǎi: impermanence marks the conditioned, suffering the tainted, non-self all phenomena, and peace the unconditioned.

quiz.q: What three reasons does the treatise give for the name udāna?
options: it teaches meaning in accord with the dharma; sages of still mind have always repeated it; this track leads to the great birth and beyond the highest existence
quiz.why: It teaches meaning in accord with the dharma; the sages of still mind have always repeated it; and this track leads to the great birth and beyond the highest existence. Venerable Miào Jìng: "muni" means stillness; a "track" is the footprints left on the road you have walked.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi summarise the cause and nature of past, present, and future formations?
options: past: neither cause nor result findable; present: result exists, cause already used up; future: cause exists, result not yet produced
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the past having perished, neither cause nor result is findable; the present has its result, the cause already spent; the future has its cause, the result not yet produced — as a seed becomes a sprout, and the sprout is no longer the seed.

quiz.q: "Death and birth are simultaneous" — what images does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: like the two ends of a scale rising and falling at once; like a revolving door — this life's aggregates pushed into the past, the next life's coming forward
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at death, death and birth are simultaneous, like the two ends of a scale going down and up at the same moment; like pushing a revolving door — this life's aggregates pass into the past as the next life's come forward.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define "ageing" among the four marks?
options: the already-arisen activity differing from the previously ceased instant
quiz.why: "This already-arisen activity, differing from the previously ceased instant, is correctly observed as ageing." Venerable Miào Jìng: everything appearing is new, nothing old.

quiz.q: Based on having/no share, three marks are set up, abiding and ageing merged as the third. How do the lectures explain this?
options: both: birth, change, cessation — abiding merged into change; Cháng Bǎi adds that change has marks, cessation none
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "birth, change, cessation" merges abiding into change; change and cessation look alike, but change has marks while cessation has none. Venerable Miào Jìng: abiding is combined into change.

quiz.q: Refuting a separate real "birth," the treatise speaks of "birth of the activity" and "birth of birth." Whom does it refute, and what are these called?
options: the Sarvāstivāda — Cháng Bǎi: they call activity-birth the "great birth," birth-of-birth the "small birth"; Miào Jìng: the great birth produces all conditioned things
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Sarvāstivādins call activity-birth the "great birth" and birth-of-birth the "small birth." Venerable Miào Jìng: the great birth produces all conditioned things, but in their view it too has its own substance.
